Japan's tax-free shopping changes on November 1, 2026 🛍️

New way:
1️⃣ Pay full price (tax included) at the store
2️⃣ Customs checks your items at the airport, before bag drop
3️⃣ The tax comes back after that

✔️ ¥5,000+ before tax, per store, per day
✔️ Keep your items with you until the customs check
✔️ Don't open or use them in Japan. Used items aren't refunded
✔️ Passport + receipts, and do it within 90 days of purchase

How the money comes back depends on the shop, so ask at the register.
Source: Japan Tourism Agency

Iekei ramen (家系) = Yokohama-style pork & soy broth with thick noodles. After you buy your ticket, they'll ask 3 things:

🍜 Noodles: katame (firm) / futsū (normal) / yawarakame (soft)
🧂 Flavor: koime (strong) / usume (light)
💧 Oil: ōme (more) / sukuname (less)

First time? Just say "futsū de" = everything normal.

Save before your first bowl. Follow for a real Tokyo lunch every week.

That charge on your izakaya bill for food you didn't order? It's "otōshi" (お通し).

🥢 A small starter served when you sit down
💴 Usually a few hundred yen per person (fancier places charge more)
🙅 You can't really send it back, but there's no tipping in Japan
🗣️ Ask first: "Otōshi-dai, arimasu ka?" = Is there a seat charge?

My 3 lunch rules as a Japanese office worker in Akihabara 🍱

1. Skip 12:00. All of Tokyo eats at noon. Go at 11:30 or after 13:00
2. Ticket machine (券売機) at the door = fast, cheap, no Japanese needed
3. Order the teishoku (定食). Rice, miso soup and pickles come with it

On the way out: "Gochisōsama deshita" = thanks for the meal.

Follow for a real Tokyo lunch every week 🐕

3 things most tourists miss at conveyor sushi 🍣

1️⃣ The green powder at your seat is tea. Add hot water from the tap at the counter
2️⃣ The pink ginger (gari) is free. Eat it between pieces, not on top
3️⃣ Don't wait for the belt. Order fresh from the touch screen (most have English)

Tokyo's real fast food: standing soba 🍜

1. Buy a ticket (shokken) at the machine by the door
2. Hand it over. If they ask: "soba" (buckwheat) or "udon" (thick wheat)
3. Eat standing. About 5 minutes
4. Put your bowl back on the counter

Cheap, fast, and no Japanese needed.

🍺 "Toriaezu nama" = a draft beer for now
🙋 "Sumimasen!" (hand up) = excuse me, to call staff

How to order sake without the menu panic 🍶

📏 Ichigō (一合) = 180 ml, good for 1–2 people
🌡️ Reishu = chilled / Atsukan = hot
👅 Karakuchi = dry / Amakuchi = sweet
🤷 Still lost? "Osusume wa?" = What do you recommend?

How to open a konbini onigiri without ripping the seaweed 🍙

1️⃣ Pull tab 1 straight down the middle
2️⃣ Pull corners 2 and 3 out to the sides
✨ Crispy seaweed, no mess

Save this for your first convenience store run 🐕

Can't read the ramen ticket machine? 🍜

👆 The top-left button is usually the shop's signature bowl
💴 Money in first, then press the button (change comes out below)
🔤 Many machines have an "EN" button
🎫 Hand the ticket to the staff and sit down

Some of the best fried chicken in Japan is next to the convenience store register 🍗

🔥 Warm glass case by the register: fried chicken, croquettes and more
👉 You can't grab it yourself. Point and say "kore kudasai" (this one, please)
🍢 In winter, look for the oden pot too

Save this for a late-night snack 🐕

#konbini #japanesefood #tokyofood #tokyonight #japantravel

Great Japanese food for less: depachika before closing 🍱

🏬 Depachika (デパ地下) = department store basement food hall
⏰ In the last hour or so, many counters add discount stickers
🏷️ Look for 割引 (waribiki) = discount

Take it back to your hotel. Best cheap dinner in Tokyo.

#depachika #tokyofood #bento #japanesefood #tokyotravel

Card or cash? Ask before you order 💳

🗣️ "Kādo tsukaemasu ka?" = Can I use a card?
💴 "Genkin dake" = cash only
🏧 Keep a few thousand yen on you. Konbini ATMs work with most foreign cards

How to eat tsukemen (dipping noodles) 🍜

1️⃣ Dip the noodles in the thick soup and eat
2️⃣ When the noodles are gone, ask for "sūpu-wari" (スープ割り). They add hot broth
3️⃣ Now drink the soup

📍 My pick: Tsujita (つじ田), near Suehirocho by Akihabara

Food allergy? Learn this before you fly to Japan ⚠️

🗣️ "___ ga taberaremasen" (〇〇が食べられません) = I can't eat ___
🦐 ebi = shrimp · 🦀 kani = crab · 🐖 butaniku = pork
📝 For serious allergies, carry it written in Japanese and show the staff

Share this with your travel buddy.

#foodallergy #japantravel #japantips #learnjapanese #tokyofood

Vegetarian in Japan? Read this 🥢

Most soups and noodle broths use dashi (だし), a stock often made from bonito fish. That includes miso soup, udon, soba and many sauces.

🗣️ Ask: "Dashi ni sakana wa haitte imasu ka?" = Is there fish in the stock?

The first question at every Tokyo restaurant 🚪

🗣️ "Nan-mei sama desu ka?" (何名様ですか) = How many people?
✋ Hold up your fingers, or say: hitori (1), futari (2), sannin (3)
🪑 Then wait to be seated

3 things that are free at Tokyo restaurants 🙌

💧 Water or tea ("mizu" if it doesn't come)
🧻 Oshibori (おしぼり), a wet towel for your hands
🙇 The service. No tipping in Japan

Don't wait for the bill at your table in Japan 🧾

📄 At most casual places, the bill is already on your table or comes with the food
🚪 Take it to the register (レジ, "reji") by the door and pay there
💴 Don't leave cash on the table. They'll chase you to give it back

🏢 Go to the station building. The top floors are the restaurant floor (レストラン街)
🍱 Many places serve the local specialty, with food samples and picture menus
😌 Not a hidden gem, but you'll eat well and won't get lost

Ameyoko (Ueno) street food rule 🍢

🧍 Eat at the stall. Many shops ask you not to eat while walking
🗣️ "Koko de tabete ii desu ka?" = Can I eat here?
🗑️ Give your trash back to the shop. There are almost no bins

Free refills at some tonkatsu shops 🍚

Not everywhere, but at some tonkatsu shops rice and cabbage refills are free. If staff are walking around with cabbage, that's the sign.

🗣️ "Okawari" (おかわり) = another one, please

Conveyor sushi: the plate color is the price 🍣

🎨 Find the color chart on the wall or menu
🍽️ Stack your plates. Staff count them at the end
💸 Gold and black plates are usually the expensive ones
